Create a validated analysis configuration

Source: R/project.R
mm_project.Rd

The analysis plan, written down and checked before anything is fitted. Every later step reads this object, so no step has to guess and no two steps can quietly disagree.

Usage

mm_project(
  slug,
  outcome,
  predictors,
  positive_class = NULL,
  cohort = NULL,
  split_var = NULL,
  split_at = NULL,
  cluster_id = NULL,
  nonlinear = NULL,
  interactions = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  knots = 4L,
  seed = 1978L
)

Arguments

slug

Short study identifier, used in artifact paths.

outcome

Length-one character naming the outcome column.

predictors

Character vector of candidate predictor columns. The order is kept, because it is the order a report presents them in.

positive_class

Optional value naming the event level of outcome. Checked against the observed values when cohort is supplied, because an inverted positive class silently inverts every reported risk.

cohort

Optional data frame. When supplied, every column named here must exist in it, the outcome must vary, and positive_class must be one of the outcome's observed values. The cohort itself is not stored.

split_var

Optional length-one character naming the column that separates development from held-out data, most often a year.

split_at

Optional single value. Rows with split_var < split_at are development and the rest are held out.

cluster_id

Optional length-one character naming the column that identifies repeated observations on one patient, for clustered resampling.

nonlinear

Optional character vector of continuous predictors to fit with restricted cubic splines. Part of the plan rather than of the fitting call, because how many degrees of freedom a continuous predictor is given is a prespecified choice: section 78 of the specification asks the configuration to carry the spline and interaction terms, and a plan that lives in whichever mm_model() call ran is not one a reviewer can check against a protocol. Left NULL the project records no shape, which is not the same as recording that every continuous predictor is straight: mm_model() then takes its own argument without calling it a departure, because there is no plan to depart from. mm_splines() shows what the choice is worth before it is written down.

interactions

Optional list of length-two character vectors naming prespecified interaction blocks. Exploratory discovery is not this argument; mm_interactions() reports evidence and selects nothing.

reference

Optional named list giving the comparison category for categorical predictors, as list(sex = "male"). Under treatment contrasts the first level is the baseline every other coefficient for that predictor is measured against, and factor() makes it the alphabetically first value unless someone says otherwise. That is a reporting decision taken by a sort order, so it belongs in the plan beside the spline and interaction terms. Declaring it also fixes the baseline against a level being lost: mm_model() refuses a declared reference that no eligible row carries, rather than quietly measuring against the next level along.

knots

Knots for each spline term.

seed

Single whole number, recorded here so that a later resampling step cannot invent one of its own.

Value

An object of class mm_project.

Details

Nothing is fitted and no row is modelled. mm_project() records choices and fails closed on combinations that cannot be meant. That is the point: the configuration is what a reviewer should be able to check against the protocol, rather than reconstruct afterwards from whichever code ran.

Examples

mm_project("uds", "event", c("age", "bmi", "sex"))
#> <mm_project: uds>
#>   outcome    event
#>   predictors 3: age, bmi, sex
#>   split      none
#>   shape      every continuous predictor linear
#>   seed       1978

# Temporal validation: develop before 2023, hold out 2023 onwards.
mm_project("uds", "event", c("age", "bmi"),
           split_var = "year", split_at = 2023)
#> <mm_project: uds>
#>   outcome    event
#>   predictors 2: age, bmi
#>   split      year < 2023 develops, the rest is held out
#>   shape      every continuous predictor linear
#>   seed       1978
